div.head: VI Atr Lat 37
div.ab: K. Si quis demonico instinctu regem circumuenire molitur, illum dignum morte iudicauimus, nisi forte maximo iuramento uel feruente ferro excusetur.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)

Steenstrup Danelag 226 vermutet hinter dem nicht genannten Beweismittel den Zweikampf (s. d. Gl 5), den er als besonders Dänische Reinigung erweist aus Hincmars Bericht vom Dänen, der in Frankreich 863 eine Anklage auf infidelitatem beweist secundum gentis sue morem cum eo negante armis coram rege contendens, ed. Mon. Germ., SS. I 462. Ein Personalrecht (s. d. Gl) seh ich aber nicht hierin, sondern territorialisiertes Partikularrecht der Denalagu; s. d. Gl 1b. 11j

Steenstrup Danelag 226 conjectures that the unnamed means of proof is the judicial combat (see that word in Gl 5), which he shows to be a specifically Danish form of purgation from Hincmar’s account of the Dane who in France in 863 proves a charge of infidelitatem secundum gentis sue morem cum eo negante armis coram rege contendens, ed. Mon. Germ., SS. I 462. I see in this, however, not a personal law (see that word in Gl) but the territorialized particular law of the Denalagu; see that word in Gl 1b. 11j
